private_scoring.reward_semantics: potential complete-allocation utility conditional on acceptance; no realized settlement

selection_metadata.recommendation_rule: maximize B potential utility, then A potential utility, then lexicographic B allocation
selection_metadata.fair_alternative_rule: maximize minimum potential utility, then team total, then A utility, then lexicographic B allocation
selection_metadata.conflict_rule: overlap value >=4 and fair alternative improves A by >=3 with B utility >0
selection_metadata.low_conflict_rule: overlap value1-2 with at least one shared-valued stocked good and fair alternative improves A by <=1
selection_metadata.stratum_semantics: low_conflict retains overlapping interests; it is not a no-conflict condition
selection_metadata.selection_rule: published context order; exclude all historical semantic contexts including reversed profiles; choose six matching inventory types with distinct original A profiles per stratum
selection_metadata.advice_generation: fixed scripted legal recommendation, not a naturally generated agent message

case.sender_prompt:
Deal or No Deal allocation-proposal task. The two negotiators are Agent 0 (A) and Agent 1 (B). Divide all books, hats and balls. Your choice gives quantities you take; A takes the complement. Seek a mutually acceptable split while considering your own value. Each agent values the entire stock at10. Both agents' exact unit values are given below in every condition. Submit one complete allocation proposal or no_agreement. Utilities are potential values conditional on later acceptance; this one-choice task does not execute a settlement. There are no earlier offers or partner-message history.
Public inventory:
{"balls":3,"books":1,"hats":1}
You are Agent 0 (A).
Agent 0 (A) original unit values:
{"balls":2,"books":1,"hats":3}
Write one concise useful message to Agent 1 (B) using only your own observations. No tools or follow-up. Plain text only, at most200 words.
